BiblicalUsage: To make different, to change — and Paul uses it for the greatest change of all. Behold, I shew you a mystery; We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed, in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump. The dead are raised incorruptible and the living are changed. And Hebrews says the heavens themselves will be changed like a garment, folded up and laid aside by the One who remains the same.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe change is the promise and the threat both at once: the heavens will be folded up like a worn coat, and my body will be changed in a moment. The difference is who does the changing — God changes what He loves into what it was made to be, and I hold that the twinkling of an eye is not too fast for Him to finish what He started in me.
